nodes.title: START HERE — 3-Clip Infinite Continuation Showcase
widgets_values:
# Herrgotts H3 Infinite — 3-Clip Showcase

This workflow demonstrates the **complete approach in one queue**: native FFLF start, two direct AV-latent continuations, freeze-safe handover analysis, and **context-aligned seamless AV joining**.

### Before you queue
1. Select the H3 model / Qwen encoder / Video VAE / Audio VAE.
2. Load First Frame + one Last Frame per clip and optionally one shared `<Picture 1>` reference.
3. Enter a separate prompt for each clip.
4. Keep resolution and core sampling settings consistent.
5. Queue once. The final joins use a **4-frame video context crossfade + 15 ms audio de-click crossfade** by default.

### Extend to Clip 4+
Change Clip 3's role from final to intermediate, duplicate its continuation block for Clip 4, and add one more **Seamless AV Join**. Set only the current last join to `Final Clip`.

nodes.title: INFO — Shared model & sampling setup
widgets_values:
### Shared setup
The model, encoder, VAEs, Sigma Shift, sampler and scheduler are reused by all three clips so the chain stays consistent.

This example uses the same values as the tested workflows. SageAttention is optional. If you change resolution, model/VAE or temporal sampling behavior, make the same change for every clip.

nodes.title: INFO — Shared Qwen reference
widgets_values:
### `<Picture 1>` reference
Optional identity/style reference used by Qwen conditioning for **all three clips** in this example.

It is not the temporal continuation source. Motion and audio continuity come directly from the previous H3 AV latent.

nodes.title: INFO — Clip 1 inputs
widgets_values:
### Clip 1
**First Frame** + **Last Frame Clip 1** define the native FFLF boundaries. Enter Clip 1's action/dialogue in the Start node.

`Duration = 10 s` is only an example. The actual H3 frame count snaps to the model's valid temporal grid.

nodes.title: INFO — Clip 1 Start node
widgets_values:
### Start FFLF
This is the only clip that needs a **First Frame** input. The sampler output is both decoded for rendering/analysis and passed directly into Clip 2 as the previous AV latent.

No rendered frames are used as the continuation context.

nodes.title: INFO — Sampling block
widgets_values:
### Per-clip sampling
Each clip has its own Guider + Noise + Sampler so it can use its own prompt while sharing the same H3 model, sampler type and sigma schedule.

Clip 2 cannot sample until Clip 1's handover metadata exists, so execution naturally proceeds in sequence.

nodes.title: INFO — Handover + Stitch Ready
widgets_values:
### Automatic boundary handling
Auto Handover finds the usable phase-aligned end of Clip 1 (or applies the no-lock fallback). **Stitch Ready** trims the rendered tail to that exact effective boundary.

The Save Latent node still stores the **full** AV latent plus metadata; trimming never destroys the continuation source.

nodes.title: INFO — Clip 2 target
widgets_values:
### Clip 2 Last Frame
Load the visual endpoint you want Clip 2 to reach. The previous clip is **not** supplied as an image — its motion/audio history arrives through the direct AV latent connection.

nodes.title: INFO — Clip 2 continuation
widgets_values:
### Continue from Clip 1
Recommended settings are already selected:
- `context_frames = 22`
- `handover_mode = auto`
- `alignment_mode = phase_aligned_extended`

The Continue node may extend the actual head context backward to a canonical H3 phase. Its `actual_head_context_frames` output therefore drives the Stitch Ready **head trim** exactly.


**Prompting tip:** describe the action as continuing through the segment (for example `she continues walking`) rather than strongly instructing the model to settle into the Last Frame. Keep important dialogue away from the very end of a segment, where trimming may occur.

If unwanted background music is a problem, try appending `non_diegetic_music: N/A`. When using `<Picture 1>` for identity, explicitly describe it as the reference for the subject's facial features, clothing and body composition.

nodes.title: INFO — Clip 2 handover / output
widgets_values:
### Clip 2 becomes both output and source
Auto Handover prepares Clip 2 for Clip 3 and the Save node stores its **full latent + actual head-context length**.

The standalone `Stitch Ready` node remains useful for inspection/export. The final **Seamless AV Join** also receives Clip 2's FULL decoded render and handover metadata so a later boundary can reuse the small Safe Tail Bridge before Clip 3 begins.

nodes.title: INFO — Clip 3 target
widgets_values:
### Clip 3 Last Frame
This is the third endpoint. Change the prompt and endpoint independently while preserving the same character/environment constraints you want carried through the sequence.

nodes.title: INFO — Clip 3 / Final Clip / easy extension
widgets_values:
### Continue from Clip 2
This block is the template for every additional clip.

The standalone `Final Clip` node is optional. In the automatic chain, the final **Seamless AV Join** receives Clip 3's FULL decoded render and is set to `Final Clip`, so the reused head is removed while the complete final-keyframe landing is preserved.

To add Clip 4, duplicate this continuation block and add one more Seamless AV Join after the current combined output. Connect Clip 3's full decoded video + handover as the new join's **previous bridge source**.

nodes.title: INFO — Final clip handover
widgets_values:
### Why still analyze the final clip?
Auto Handover still runs on Clip 3 so its full latent and continuation metadata remain ready if you later extend the chain.

For the **finished 3-clip video**, `Final Clip` intentionally ignores that tail cutoff: it removes only the reused head overlap and preserves the complete final-keyframe landing.

If you add Clip 4 later, switch Clip 3 back to `Stitch Ready` and use `Final Clip` on the new last segment.

nodes.title: FINAL STEP — Automatic AV stitching
widgets_values:
# Automatic seamless AV stitching
The final stage uses the reused context that already exists around every continuation boundary.

- **Safe Tail Bridge (recommended):** H3 sometimes has 1–3 visually valid frames between the phase-aligned latent cutoff and the detector's safe ideal end. The stitcher can keep up to **2** of those exact pixels from the previous clip and skips the same number of early video frames from the next clip. It never borrows from the freeze safety margin and does not change duration.
- **Video:** after the bridge, the final **4** corresponding context frames are cosine-blended. Keep this short to avoid ghosting.
- **Audio:** the already-tested **15 ms de-click crossfade** remains independent. Safe Tail Bridge does not move the audio boundary, so A/V timing stays unchanged.
- **Boundary luminance match:** retained only as an optional experimental fallback and **OFF by default**. Earlier tests showed that gain matching could turn a hard brightness seam into a visible brightness drift.
- Clip 1/2 remain intermediate segments; the current last clip is joined as `Final Clip`, so its complete final-keyframe landing remains.

Set `max_safe_tail_bridge_frames = 0` to disable the bridge. Set either crossfade to `0` to compare against hard cuts.

nodes.title: INFO — Extending the final stitch
widgets_values:
### Adding Clip 4+
Duplicate the last continuation block and add **one more Seamless AV Join** after the current combined output.

For every new join:
1. previous images/audio = output of the preceding Seamless AV Join,
2. next images/audio = the **FULL decoded render** of the new clip,
3. next head context = `actual_head_context_frames` from that clip's Continue node,
4. next handover = that clip's Auto Handover,
5. **previous_full_images + previous_handover** = the full decoded render and handover of the clip immediately before it; these enable Safe Tail Bridge,
6. use `Stitch Ready` for intermediate clips and `Final Clip` only for the current last clip.

For very long projects, use **04 — Stitch Saved Chain** instead; it performs the same boundary logic while decoding/writing one saved clip at a time.
